CSE-1121.courseRationale: Introduces students to computer programming using structured language (C). Students enhance problem-solving skills and develop structured programs using fundamental elements.
objectives: Familiarize with basic terminologies used in computer programming.
Proficiently transform designs of problem solutions into a standard programming language.
Proficiently use fundamental programming elements: variables, data types, structures, loops, functions, console and file I/O.

clos.description: Demonstrate understanding of basic computer organization, data types, operators, I/O operations, preprocessor directives, and principles of structured programming in C.
Develop C programs using conditional statements, loops, arrays, functions, and strings to solve structured computational problems.
Apply pointers, structures, file operations, and dynamic memory allocation in C to manage and organize data efficiently.
Identify and correct syntax, logical, and runtime errors in C programs using systematic debugging and testing strategies.

midtermContent.topic: Basic computer organization, software classification; Flowcharts; C history, Identifiers, keywords, data types, constants, variables.
Operators: arithmetic, unary, relational, logical, assignment, bitwise; Precedence; I/O operations: scanf, printf, getchar, puts, formatted I/O.
Control statements: Branching (if, if-else, nested if, switch); Looping (while, do-while, for loops).

finalContent.topic: Nested Looping, break and continue statements, goto statement.
Functions: Prototypes, passing arguments, recursion, storage classes.
Arrays & Strings: Multidimensional arrays, string operations, string library functions, array of strings.
Pointers & Structures: Pointer declarations, dynamic memory allocation (malloc, calloc, free), structure, union, self-referential structure.
Files: File handling (opening, reading, writing, closing), low-level bitwise operations, macros and preprocessors.

CSE-1122.courseRationale: Hands-on implementation and practical application of concepts taught in CSE-1121 structured C programming.
objectives: Use IDEs to write, compile, and execute C programs.
Apply debugging techniques to locate and resolve errors.
Implement simple information management system using arrays, structures, and files.

clos.description: Use integrated programming environments to write, compile, execute, and debug C programs.
Apply variables, data structures, control structures, functions, pointers, and file manipulation to solve problems.
Implement an information management system using structures, functions, and file processing.

midtermContent.topic: Familiarization with C compiler, simple I/O, operators, data types, and library functions.
Decision-making techniques: if, if-else, nested if, switch statement problems.
Looping mechanisms: while, do-while, for loops, nested loops problem solving.

finalContent.topic: Functions and recursion: User-defined functions, recursion tree implementation.
1D and 2D Arrays, String manipulation and related algorithmic problem solving.
Pointers, dynamic memory allocation, and structures.
File handling and bitwise operations.
Console-based capstone project design and implementation.

textbooks.title: Theory and Problems of Programming with C

CSE-1221.courseRationale: Object Oriented Programming (OOP) using C++. Equips students with in-depth knowledge of OOP paradigm: classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, and STL.
objectives: Design, compile, and execute C++ programs to solve complex problems.
Master Object-Oriented principles: encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism.
Understand generic programming with templates and Standard Template Library (STL).

clos.description: Demonstrate understanding of basic OOP concepts (abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism).
Apply OOP features (polymorphism, inheritance, operator overloading) for problem solving.
Demonstrate proficiency in advanced C++ concepts (templates, STL containers, exception handling, stream I/O).

midtermContent.topic: Introduction to OOP vs POP, C++ Console I/O, classes and objects, access specifiers, constructors and destructors.
Object pointers, inline functions, friend functions, static member functions, arrays of objects, this pointer, new/delete.
Function overloading, constructor overloading, copy constructor, default arguments.

finalContent.topic: Operator overloading: Unary and binary operator overloading, friend operator functions.
Inheritance: Single, multiple, multilevel, hierarchical, virtual base classes, constructors in derived classes.
Virtual functions: Polymorphism, pure virtual functions, abstract classes, early and late binding.
Templates & STL: Generic functions, class templates, exception handling, STL containers (vector, list, map), iterators.
C++ I/O Stream system: Formatted and unformatted I/O, file streams, binary file operations.

CSE-1222.courseRationale: Hands-on implementation of Object-Oriented Programming in C++: classes, objects, operator overloading, inheritance, virtual functions, templates, and STL.
objectives: Design, compile, and execute C++ programs to solve basic problems.
Understand data management and control structures in C++.
Apply OOP design in building modular applications.

clos.description: Demonstrate the understanding of basic OOP concepts.
Solve real-life problems using polymorphism, inheritance, and operator overloading.
Develop applications integrating modern data handling, templates, and exception handling.

midtermContent.topic: Introduction to C++ Console I/O, classes, objects, constructor/destructor implementation.
Class arrays, pointer to objects, friend functions, and parameter passing.
Function and constructor overloading practice.

finalContent.topic: Operator overloading: Unary and binary operators.
Inheritance implementation: Single, multiple, multilevel, and hierarchical.
Virtual functions and pure virtual functions in polymorphic applications.
Templates and STL: vector, queue, stack, map, and algorithms.
C++ file handling and project implementation.

CSE-1223.courseRationale: Develops logical thinking and mathematical foundations essential for algorithm design, computer theory, and cryptography.
objectives: Obtain comprehensive knowledge in discrete structures and algebraic systems.
Understand methods of mathematical proofs and induction.
Acquire insights into applications such as coding, graphs, and tree structures.

clos.description: Apply and understand propositional and predicate logic, truth tables, and mathematical reasoning.
Apply number theory, modular arithmetic, induction, recursion, and combinatorics.
Master graph theory and tree structures and use them to model and solve computational problems.

midtermContent.topic: Set Theory: Set operations, representations, algebraic properties, computer representation of sets.
Logic: Propositional calculus, equivalences, predicates, quantifiers, rule of inference.
Functions & Relations: Types of functions, Big-O notation, relations, equivalence relations, partitions, closures.

finalContent.topic: Number Theory: Modular arithmetic, GCD, LCM, prime numbers, congruence, Chinese Remainder Theorem.
Mathematical Reasoning: Proof techniques, mathematical induction, recursive definitions.
Counting & Combinatorics: Pigeonhole principle, permutations, combinations, binomial coefficients, recurrence relations.
Graphs: Terminology, representations, isomorphism, connectivity, Euler/Hamilton paths, shortest paths, graph coloring.
Trees: Binary trees, tree traversals, spanning trees, minimal spanning trees, expression trees.

CSE-1230.courseRationale: Encourages students to enhance problem solving, algorithmic thinking, and competitive programming speed on platforms like Codeforces (800-900 rating).
objectives: Introduce students to algorithmic problem solving by computers.
Help students enhance analytical skills and contest coding speed.
Foster creativity and innovation under contest time constraints.

clos.description: Apply conditional statements, arrays, basic number theory, and STL to solve competitive problems.
Demonstrate competency in solving moderately difficult contest problems (Codeforces 800-900 rating).

midtermContent.topic: Input/Output optimization, fast I/O, conditional logic, loops and arrays problem-solving.
String operations, pattern matching, Standard Template Library (vector, string, queue, stack, map).
Number theory basics: Primality test, GCD, LCM, modular arithmetic.

finalContent.topic: Recursion, recursion trees, and polynomial vs logarithmic time complexity analysis.
Binary search on answers and fractions, lower bound, upper bound.
Prefix sums, two-pointer approach, sorting comparators, greedy algorithms.

referenceBooks.authors: Steven S. Skiena, Miguel A. Revilla
referenceBooks.title: Programming Challenges

CSE-2321.courseRationale: Core foundational course in computing. Covers linear and non-linear data structures, memory representations, time-space efficiency, and selection of optimal structures for real-world problems.
objectives: Understand linear structures: linked lists, arrays, stacks, queues and applications.
Understand non-linear structures: trees, heaps, graphs and traversal algorithms.
Familiarize with sorting, searching, hashing, and performance tradeoffs.

clos.description: Describe operations of linear and non-linear data structures along with time and space complexity.
Apply appropriate data structures to solve computational engineering problems.
Analyze performance tradeoffs of algorithms and data structures.

midtermContent.topic: Introduction: Elementary data organization, data structure operations, time-space tradeoffs, Big-O notation, pattern matching.
Arrays: Linear arrays, 2D arrays, sparse matrices, bubble sort, linear and binary search.
Linked Lists: Singly linked lists, doubly linked lists, circular lists, header lists, operations.

finalContent.topic: Stacks: Array and pointer representation, push/pop, infix to postfix conversion, postfix expression evaluation.
Queues: Linear queue, circular queue, priority queues, deques, recursion and Tower of Hanoi.
Algorithm Complexity & Sorting: Quick sort, merge sort, insertion sort, selection sort, hashing and collision resolution.
Trees: Binary search trees (BST), insertion, deletion, AVL trees, heaps, heapsort, B-trees.
Graphs: Graph representations (adjacency matrix, adjacency list), BFS, DFS traversal algorithms.

referenceBooks.authors: Y. Langsam, M. Augenstein, A.M. Tanenbaum
referenceBooks.title: Data Structures Using C and C++

CSE-2322.courseRationale: Practical programming implementation of linear and non-linear data structures in C/C++.
objectives: Implement linked lists, stacks, queues, and tree structures in code.
Compare sorting and searching algorithms experimentally.
Develop an application project utilizing multiple data structures.

clos.description: Apply basic concepts of linear data structures for solving different problems.
Apply non-linear data structures for manipulating hierarchical and connected data.
Develop an application project addressing several data structures.

midtermContent.topic: Array operations, linear search, binary search, bubble sort, insertion sort.
Linked lists: Singly, doubly, and circular linked list implementations.
Stack operations, infix-to-postfix expression evaluation.

finalContent.topic: Queue implementations: Linear, circular, priority queue.
Binary Search Tree (BST) creation, insertion, deletion, and traversals.
Graph representation and BFS, DFS traversals.
Comprehensive data structure project submission and defense.

CSE-2323.courseRationale: Covers logic design of digital electronic circuits: Boolean algebra, combinational logic (adders, decoders, multiplexers), sequential circuits (flip-flops, registers, counters), and register transfer logic.
objectives: Understand number systems, binary codes, Boolean algebra, and logic gates.
Design combinational circuits: adders, subtractors, multiplexers, decoders.
Analyze clocked sequential circuits: flip-flops, state reduction, counters, and registers.

clos.description: Understand number systems, Boolean algebra, and combinational/sequential logic circuits.
Interpret and simplify Boolean expressions using K-maps, truth tables, and state tables.
Analyze and implement digital circuits: adders, comparators, decoders, ROM, PLA, counters, and registers.

midtermContent.topic: Binary Systems & Boolean Algebra: Number systems, binary codes, logic gates, canonical forms.
Simplification: K-maps (2 to 6 variables), NAND/NOR implementation, don't care conditions, exclusive-OR.
Combinational Logic: Design procedure, adders, subtractors, code converters.

finalContent.topic: MSI & LSI Logic: Look-ahead carry adder, magnitude comparator, decoders, encoders, multiplexers.
Sequential Logic: Flip-flops (SR, JK, D, T), triggering, clocked sequential circuits, state reduction.
Registers & Counters: Shift registers, ripple counters, synchronous counters, RAM, ROM, PLA.
Processor Logic Design: Register transfer, arithmetic-logic unit (ALU) design, accumulator design.

CSE-2421.courseRationale: Introduces design paradigms and analytical techniques for algorithms: divide-and-conquer, greedy, dynamic programming, and complexity classes.
objectives: Demonstrate familiarity with major algorithms and data structures.
Analyze algorithms for deriving mathematical proofs of correctness and asymptotic performance.
Synthesize efficient algorithms using standard design paradigms.

clos.description: Demonstrate familiarity with algorithm design paradigms, sorting, searching, and tree/graph algorithms.
Analyze time and space complexity, asymptotic notations, and construct rigorous correctness proofs.
Apply graph algorithms to model and solve engineering problems.
Design and implement efficient algorithms using divide-and-conquer, greedy, dynamic programming, and backtracking.

midtermContent.topic: Algorithm analysis: Growth of functions, asymptotic notations, solving recurrences (master theorem, recursion tree, substitution).
Divide and Conquer: Merge sort, quicksort, heap sort, linear-time sorting (counting sort, radix sort).
Dynamic Programming: Elements of DP, memoization, matrix-chain multiplication, Longest Common Subsequence (LCS).

finalContent.topic: Greedy Algorithms: Activity selection, Huffman codes, fractional knapsack, string matching (Naive, Rabin-Karp).
Graph Algorithms: BFS, DFS, Minimum Spanning Trees (Kruskal, Prim), topological sort.
Shortest Paths: Dijkstra's algorithm, Bellman-Ford algorithm, Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest path.
Computational Geometry & Number Theory: Convex hull (Graham scan), GCD, modular arithmetic, prime numbers.
NP-Completeness: Classes P, NP, NP-Complete, Cook-Levin theorem, backtracking (N-Queen), branch and bound.

textbooks.authors: T.H. Cormen, C.E. Leiserson, R.L. Rivest, C. Stein
textbooks.title: Introduction to Algorithms

CSE-2423.courseRationale: Provides foundational principles to design, implement, and manage relational databases: ER modeling, relational algebra, SQL, normalization, transactions, and concurrency.
objectives: Familiarize with relational databases, data modeling, storage, and transaction management.
Apply relational algebra, SQL queries, optimization, security, and normalization techniques.
Design an enterprise data model conforming to business constraints.

clos.description: Understand relational databases, database architectures, storage, querying, and transactions.
Apply relational algebra, SQL, normalization (1NF-BCNF), and ACID properties.
Create an enterprise entity-relationship data model reflecting organizational business rules.

midtermContent.topic: Introduction: Database vs file systems, data models, database architecture, storage manager.
Entity-Relationship (ER) Model: Entities, relationships, mapping cardinalities, keys, ER diagrams, specialization, generalization.
Relational Algebra and SQL: Select, project, union, join, division, aggregate functions, nested subqueries, views.

finalContent.topic: Integrity & Security: Constraints, assertions, triggers, authorization, encryption, security roles.
Functional Dependencies & Normalization: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF, closure of attributes.
Indexing & Hashing: B+ tree index files, hash functions, static and dynamic hashing.
Transactions: ACID properties, serializability, recoverability, shadow copy, cascadeless schedules.
Concurrency Control & Recovery: Two-phase locking, deadlock detection, timestamp protocols, checkpoints.

textbooks.authors: A. Silberschatz, H.F. Korth, S. Sudarshan
textbooks.title: Database System Concepts

referenceBooks.authors: Hector Garcia-Molina, Jeff Ullman, Jennifer Widom
referenceBooks.title: Database Systems: The Complete Book

CSE-2427.courseRationale: Foundational understanding of computation: automata models, formal grammars, Turing machines, decidability, computability, and complexity classes.
objectives: Learn formal mathematical models of computation and relationships with formal languages.
Distinguish and classify computing languages in the Chomsky hierarchy.
Understand theoretical limits of computation and unsolvable problems.

clos.description: Demonstrate knowledge of different mathematical models of computation and relation to formal languages.
Design finite automata (DFA/NFA), pushdown automata (PDA), and Turing machines.
Analyze computability, decidability, P vs NP, and reduction techniques.

midtermContent.topic: Regular Languages: Finite automata, DFA, NFA, equivalence of NFA and DFA, regular operations, regular expressions.
Pumping Lemma for regular languages, non-regular languages.

finalContent.topic: Context-Free Languages: Context-free grammars (CFG), ambiguity, Chomsky normal form, Pushdown Automata (PDA).
Computability Theory: Church-Turing thesis, Turing machines, decidability, Halting problem, diagonalization.
Complexity Theory: Classes P, NP, NP-Completeness, Cook-Levin theorem, polynomial time reductions.

textbooks.title: Introduction to the Theory of Computation

textbooks.authors: J.E. Hopcroft, R. Motwani, J.D. Ullman
textbooks.title: Introduction to Automata Theory, Languages, and Computation

referenceBooks.title: An Introduction to Formal Languages and Automata

CSE-3521.courseRationale: Covers design, structure, and performance of computer hardware: datapath, control unit, pipelining, memory hierarchy, cache organization, and I/O interfacing.
objectives: Understand CPU architecture, memory hierarchy, and peripherals.
Analyze MIPS instruction formats, addressing modes, and single/multi-cycle datapaths.
Master pipelining, hazards, and branch prediction mechanisms.

clos.description: Understand basic organization of computers, instruction formats, addressing modes, and processor architectures.
Analyze performance metrics, memory hierarchy, I/O transfer modes, DMA, and interrupts.
Illustrate CPU working, datapath, and control signals during instruction execution.

midtermContent.topic: Computer architecture basics, MIPS performance evaluation, CPU execution time, MIPS as performance measure.
Instruction set principles: MIPS 32-bit addressing, instruction formats (R-type, I-type, J-type), operands.
Arithmetic & Logic: ALU design, signed/unsigned arithmetic, floating-point hardware representation.

finalContent.topic: Control Unit: Single-cycle datapath, control signal generation, multi-cycle implementation.
Pipelining: Pipelining overview, data hazards, structural hazards, control hazards, pipeline control.
Memory Organization: Memory hierarchy, cache memory, cache hits/misses, placement policies, virtual memory.
I/O Systems: Direct Memory Access (DMA), interrupts, buses, RAID configurations.

textbooks.authors: John L. Hennessy, David A. Patterson
textbooks.title: Computer Organization and Design

CSE-3527.courseRationale: Covers compiler phases: lexical analysis, syntax analysis (LL and LR parsers), syntax-directed translation, intermediate code generation, and optimization.
objectives: Understand compiler construction fundamentals and phases.
Master parsing techniques: Top-down (LL1) and Bottom-up (SLR, LALR, CLR).
Implement code optimization and target code generation.

clos.description: Understand modern compiler construction concepts and architecture.
Apply theory of computation and automata for scanner and parser design.
Analyze lexical, syntax, semantic phases, and syntax-directed translation.
Evaluate code generation and optimization techniques.
Design structured compiler phases using standard compiler construction tools.

midtermContent.topic: Structure of compiler: Phases, passes, front-end and back-end, compiler tools.
Grammars: Context-free grammars, derivations, parse trees, ambiguity.
Lexical Analysis: Regular expressions, transition diagrams, DFA, symbol table management.

finalContent.topic: Top-Down Parsing: Left recursion elimination, left factoring, FIRST and FOLLOW sets, LL(1) parsing.
Bottom-Up Parsing: Shift-reduce parsing, operator precedence, LR parsers (SLR, CLR, LALR).
Syntax-Directed Translation: Semantic rules, synthesized/inherited attributes, syntax trees.
Intermediate Code Generation: Three-address code, quadruples, triples, indirect triples.
Code Optimization & Generation: Basic blocks, flow graphs, peephole optimization, loop optimization.

textbooks.authors: A.V. Aho, M.S. Lam, R. Sethi, J.D. Ullman
textbooks.title: Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools

CSE-3532.courseTitle: Tools and Technologies for Internet Programming
CSE-3532.courseRationale: Practical experience designing and deploying full-stack web applications: HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript, React, Node.js, Express, MongoDB, and PostgreSQL.
objectives: Understand architecture and protocols of modern web systems.
Build interactive, responsive UIs using Tailwind CSS and React.
Develop secure RESTful backend APIs with Node.js, Express, and databases.

clos.description: Demonstrate proficiency in front-end and back-end web tools and structured development.
Apply foundational web technologies (HTML, CSS, JS, DOM) in project environments.
Design secure, full-stack web systems addressing security, authentication, and state management.
Implement complete full-stack web apps with modern frameworks and database integration.

midtermContent.topic: Web overview, HTTP, HTML5 semantic structure, forms, and CSS fundamentals.
Tailwind CSS: Utility-first styling, responsive design, components.
JavaScript: ES6+ syntax, arrays, objects, DOM manipulation, and event handling.

finalContent.topic: React.js: Components, JSX, props, state, hooks (useState, useEffect), React Router.
Authentication: JWT tokens, Firebase Auth, login/registration workflows.
Node.js & Express: REST APIs, middleware, routing, CORS, environment variables.
Database Integration: MongoDB (Mongoose) and PostgreSQL (Sequelize/Prisma).
Comprehensive Full-Stack capstone project development and live deployment.

textbooks.title: Internet & World Wide Web: How to Program

CSE-3631.courseRationale: Operating systems mediate hardware and software interactions. Covers process management, CPU scheduling, synchronization, deadlocks, memory management, and file systems.
objectives: Understand OS services, system calls, and kernel architectures.
Analyze process scheduling, concurrency, synchronization, and deadlock prevention.
Examine paging, segmentation, virtual memory, and disk scheduling algorithms.

clos.description: Explain fundamental principles and core services provided by an operating system.
Analyze and evaluate scheduling algorithms, synchronization mechanisms, and deadlock management.
Evaluate memory management, paging, virtual memory, and file/disk structures.

midtermContent.topic: OS overview: Services, system calls, system programs, OS design and architecture, virtual machines.
Process Management: Process states, PCB, process scheduling, CPU scheduling algorithms, threads, IPC.
Process Synchronization: Critical section problem, race condition, mutex locks, semaphores, monitors.

finalContent.topic: Deadlock: Characterization, prevention, avoidance (Banker's algorithm), detection and recovery.
Memory Management: Logical vs physical address, MMU, continuous allocation, paging, segmentation, swapping.
Virtual Memory: Demand paging, page replacement algorithms (FIFO, LRU, Optimal), thrashing.
File Systems: Access methods, directory structure, file-system mounting, allocation methods.
Protection & Security: Domain of protection, access matrix, access control lists, system threats.

textbooks.authors: Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin, Greg Gagne
textbooks.title: Operating System Concepts

CSE-3633.courseRationale: Layered computer networking architecture: LAN/WAN, routing, transport layer (TCP/UDP), and modern application protocols.
objectives: Understand network architecture, switching, and routing protocols.
Master IP addressing, CIDR, VLSM, subnetting, and network address translation (NAT).
Examine TCP flow/congestion control and application layer services (HTTP, DNS, TLS).

clos.description: Understand and analyze network architectures, link-layer protocols, and network layers.
Evaluate performance of transport and routing protocols.
Demonstrate familiarity with network routing, flow control, and security protocols.
Apply network solutions to real-world communication systems.

midtermContent.topic: Network models: OSI and TCP/IP architecture, Link layer protocols, Pure ALOHA, Slotted ALOHA.
CSMA, CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA, wireless networks (IEEE 802.11, Bluetooth, WSN).
Network Layer: Packet switching, IPv4 addressing, subnetting, CIDR, VLSM, NAT.

finalContent.topic: IPv6 representation, routing algorithms (Link State, Distance Vector).
Congestion control, QoS, routing protocols (RIP, OSPF, BGP), ICMP, ARP.
Transport Layer: Port addresses, connection establishment/release, multiplexing.
TCP: Connection lifecycle, sliding window, flow control, congestion control, UDP datagrams.
Application Layer: Client-server paradigm, HTTP, DNS, SMTP, CDN, Peer-to-Peer networks.

CSE-3635.courseRationale: Explores foundational and modern AI principles: intelligent agents, heuristic search, game playing, logic inference, probabilistic reasoning, and machine learning.
objectives: Understand foundations of AI and agent architectures.
Apply heuristic search (A*, Hill Climbing, Genetic Algorithms) and adversarial game search.
Understand knowledge representation, first-order logic, and machine learning basics.

clos.description: Identify key components of AI agents and environmental interactions.
Demonstrate informed and heuristic search algorithms, game playing, and constraint satisfaction.
Apply AI techniques for knowledge representation, first-order logic, and probabilistic reasoning.
Analyze decision-making, expert systems, and machine learning methods.

midtermContent.topic: Introduction to AI, history, state-of-the-art, problem formulation, problem-solving agents.
Searching Techniques: Informed search, A* search, greedy search, Hill Climbing, Simulated Annealing, Genetic Algorithms.
Game Playing & CSP: Alpha-Beta pruning, Constraint Satisfaction Problems (TSP, graph coloring).

finalContent.topic: Propositional & First-Order Logic: Inference rules, resolution, forward/backward chaining.
Probabilistic Reasoning: Bayes rule, Bayesian networks, certainty factors, fuzzy logic.
Expert Systems: Knowledge representation, rule-based systems, expert system shells.
Learning: Inductive learning, decision trees, neural network learning.
Natural Language Processing: Syntactic processing, semantic analysis, discourse processing.

CSE-4743.courseRationale: Covers computer and network security: cryptography, symmetric/asymmetric ciphers (RSA, AES), hashing (SHA-3), IPsec, firewalls, and security policies.
objectives: Understand network security models and cryptographic foundations.
Apply digital signatures, public key infrastructure, and secure protocols.
Examine firewall design, intrusion detection systems, and threat mitigation.

clos.description: Identify concepts of computer security, symmetric and asymmetric cryptography.
Apply cryptographic techniques: RSA, digital signatures, PGP, S/MIME.
Evaluate IP security architectures and transport layer security (TLS).
Apply firewall design principles and intrusion detection systems.

midtermContent.topic: Computer security concepts, security attacks, services, and security mechanism model.
Symmetric Ciphers: Substitution, transposition, block ciphers, DES, AES data encryption.
Euclid's algorithm, traffic confidentiality, and secret key distribution.

finalContent.topic: Public Key Cryptography & RSA: Prime numbers, Euler's theorem, RSA algorithm, Diffie-Hellman key exchange.
Cryptographic Hash Functions: SHA-3, digital signatures, Kerberos, X.509 certificates, PGP, S/MIME.
IP Security & Web Security: IPsec, ESP, TLS/SSL transport layer security.
Wireless & System Security: Firewalls, IDS/IPS, cloud security controls, privacy, and blockchain.

textbooks.title: Cryptography and Network Security: Principles and Practice

CSE-4877.coRequisite: CSE-4878 (Machine Learning and Data Mining Lab)
CSE-4877.courseRationale: Broad introduction to machine learning and data mining: data preprocessing, classification (decision trees, SVM, neural networks), clustering (K-means, DBSCAN), and evaluation.
objectives: Critically evaluate technical and algorithmic issues of building ML applications.
Apply state-of-the-art tools and techniques to solve real-world predictive modeling problems.

clos.description: Remember statistical data analysis techniques and data mining functionality.
Understand and apply data preprocessing, cleaning, transformation, and feature reduction.
Apply machine learning algorithms for classification and clustering.
Analyze and evaluate different ML and DM algorithms, ensemble methods, and outliers.

midtermContent.topic: Introduction: Data mining functionality, classification of DM systems, top-10 algorithms.
Data Objects, attribute types, statistical descriptions, measuring similarity and distance.
Data Preprocessing: Data cleaning, integration, reduction, transformation, frequent itemset mining.

finalContent.topic: Data Warehouse Modeling: Data cubes, OLAP operations, linear regression.
Classification: Decision tree induction, Naive Bayes, model evaluation metrics (ROC, F1-score).
Advanced Classification: Ensemble methods (Random Forest, Boosting), Backpropagation, SVM.
Cluster Analysis: Partitioning (K-means, K-medoids), hierarchical methods, density-based (DBSCAN).
Outlier Detection: Contextual, collective, and density-based anomaly detection.

CSE-3641.courseRationale: Provides a comprehensive study of computer networks principles, protocol layering (OSI & TCP/IP), network architecture, packet switching, routing algorithms, transport layer congestion control, and application layer protocols.
objectives: Understand layered network architectures and protocol models (OSI 7-layer and TCP/IP).
Analyze data communication mechanisms, framing, error control, and medium access protocols.
Evaluate routing algorithms, IP addressing (IPv4/IPv6), subnetting, TCP/UDP mechanisms, and congestion management.

clos.description: Explain foundational network models, protocol hierarchies, transmission media, and switching techniques.
Analyze data link layer framing, error detection/correction, and MAC sublayer protocols (Ethernet, CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA).
Design network subnets (CIDR, VLSM) and configure routing algorithms (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, OSPF, BGP).
Evaluate transport layer protocols (TCP flow/congestion control, UDP) and network application protocols (DNS, HTTP, SMTP).

midtermContent.topic: Introduction: Network types (LAN, MAN, WAN), network topologies, reference models (OSI and TCP/IP protocol suites).
Physical Layer: Transmission media (guided/unguided), digital transmission, multiplexing (FDM, TDM, WDM), packet switching vs circuit switching.
Data Link Layer: Framing, error detection and correction (Parity, Checksum, CRC, Hamming codes), Flow and Error control (Stop-and-Wait, Go-Back-N, Selective Repeat).

finalContent.topic: Medium Access Control (MAC): Random access protocols (ALOHA, CSMA, CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA), Ethernet standards, token ring, wireless LAN (IEEE 802.11).
Network Layer: Logical addressing (IPv4 classes, CIDR, subnetting, supernetting, IPv6), Address resolution (ARP, RARP), DHCP, ICMP, NAT.
Routing Principles & Algorithms: Unicast routing, Link State (OSPF), Distance Vector (RIP), Path Vector (BGP), hierarchical routing.
Transport Layer: Process-to-process delivery, UDP, TCP three-way handshake, flow control (sliding window), congestion control algorithms (Slow Start, Congestion Avoidance).
Application Layer: Domain Name System (DNS), HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, Email protocols (SMTP, POP3, IMAP), network security fundamentals.

textbooks.authors: Andrew S. Tanenbaum, David J. Wetherall
textbooks.title: Computer Networks

referenceBooks.authors: James F. Kurose, Keith W. Ross

Cisco Packet Tracer basics: Peer-to-peer network, Star topology with switches and routers.
Subnetting implementation (VLSM) and Static Routing configuration on Cisco routers.

finalContent.topic: Dynamic Routing: Configuring RIP and OSPF on multi-router topologies.
VLAN and Inter-VLAN Routing (Router-on-a-Stick) configuration.
Wireshark packet sniffing: HTTP, DNS, TCP Handshake, ARP analysis.
Socket Programming: Implementing TCP Echo Server and UDP Chat Application.

textbooks.title: Data Communications and Networking Lab Manual

CSE-4741.courseRationale: Covers the theoretical foundations and engineering implementation of modern compilers and interpreters: lexical analysis, syntax analysis, syntax-directed translation, intermediate code generation, code optimization, and target machine code generation.
objectives: Understand compiler architecture and the phases of translation from source to target code.
Master parsing algorithms (LL(1), LR(0), SLR(1), LALR(1), LR(1)).
Apply intermediate code generation, semantic analysis, and machine-independent optimizations.

clos.description: Formulate regular expressions, finite automata, and construct lexical analyzers using automated tools (Lex/Flex).
Construct top-down and bottom-up parsing tables for Context-Free Grammars (LL, LR, LALR).
Perform type checking, syntax-directed translation, and generate three-address code representations.
Apply control-flow analysis, data-flow optimization, loop optimization, and register allocation techniques.

midtermContent.topic: Compiler overview: Phases of compiler, cousin tools (interpreters, linkers, loaders), cross-compilers.
Lexical Analysis: Role of lexical analyzer, tokens, patterns, lexemes; Regular expressions, Thompson's construction NFA, Subset construction DFA, DFA minimization.

Syntax Analysis: Context-Free Grammars (CFG), ambiguity, left recursion removal, left factoring; Top-Down Parsing: Recursive descent, First and Follow sets, Predictive LL(1) parsing table construction.

finalContent.topic: Bottom-Up Parsing: Shift-reduce parsing, handles, viable prefixes; LR(0) items, SLR(1) parsing table construction and conflict resolution.
Canonical LR(1) and LALR(1) parsing tables, error recovery in parsers, parser generators (Yacc/Bison).
Syntax-Directed Translation (SDT): Synthesized and inherited attributes, S-attributed and L-attributed definitions; Symbol table organization and type checking.
Intermediate Code Generation: Three-address code (quadruples, triples, indirect triples), translation of boolean expressions, control flow backpatching.
Code Optimization & Generation: Basic blocks, flow graphs, DAG representation, peephole optimization, loop optimization, register allocation and code generation.

textbooks.authors: Alfred V. Aho, Monica S. Lam, Ravi Sethi, Jeffrey D. Ullman
textbooks.title: Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools (Dragon Book)

CSE-4742.courseRationale: Practical engineering of compiler components using C/C++, Flex (Lexical Analyzer Generator), and Bison/Yacc (Parser Generator).
objectives: Implement custom lexical analyzers and syntax checkers from scratch in C/C++.
Develop complete scanner and parser front-ends using Flex and Bison.
Generate intermediate code and construct simple code generator back-ends.

clos.description: Build regular expression tokenizers and symbol tables in C/C++.
Construct grammar rules, precedence definitions, and abstract syntax trees with Bison.
Generate three-address code and implement simple execution engines for custom programming languages.

midtermContent.topic: Building a custom scanner in C: whitespace stripping, identifier recognition, keyword lookup.
Introduction to Flex: Writing lex specification files (.l), rules, actions, and regular expressions.
Simulating DFA state transitions and symbol table management.

finalContent.topic: Introduction to Bison/Yacc: Grammar rules (.y), tokens integration with Flex.
Building an arithmetic expression calculator with precedence and associativity in Bison.
AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) node generation, type checking, and error reporting.
Capstone Mini-Compiler: Translating a C-subset language into Three-Address Code or assembly.

CSE-4871.courseRationale: Introduces hardware, mathematical foundations, and software algorithms for rendering 2D and 3D computer graphics: scan conversion, 2D/3D geometric transformations, viewing pipelines, clipping, illumination models, shading, and visible surface determination.
objectives: Master mathematical foundations of affine transformations (scaling, rotation, translation, shearing).
Understand rasterization algorithms: line drawing, circle drawing, polygon filling.
Explore 3D projection, hidden surface removal, Phong illumination, and ray tracing.

clos.description: Implement scan conversion algorithms for fundamental raster primitives (Bresenham, Midpoint).
Apply 2D/3D affine transformations using homogeneous coordinates and composite matrix multiplications.
Apply line and polygon clipping algorithms (Cohen-Sutherland, Liang-Barsky, Sutherland-Hodgman).
Evaluate 3D viewing, parallel/perspective projections, lighting, shading (Gouraud/Phong), and visible surface algorithms.

midtermContent.topic: Introduction: Graphics architectures, raster display systems, frame buffers, CRT and modern OLED displays.
Scan Conversion: DDA algorithm, Bresenham's line algorithm, Midpoint circle drawing algorithm, Ellipse generation.
2D Geometric Transformations: Translation, rotation, scaling, reflection, shear; Homogeneous coordinates and composite transformation matrices.

finalContent.topic: 2D Viewing & Clipping: Window-to-Viewport transformation; Line clipping (Cohen-Sutherland, Liang-Barsky), Polygon clipping (Sutherland-Hodgman), curve clipping.
3D Concepts & Transformations: 3D coordinates, 3D affine transformations, rotation about arbitrary axes.
3D Viewing Pipeline: Parallel projection (orthographic, oblique), Perspective projection (vanishing points, perspective anomalies).
Visible Surface Detection: Object-space vs image-space methods; Back-face culling, Depth-Buffer (Z-buffer) algorithm, A-buffer, Warnock algorithm.
Illumination & Shading: Ambient, diffuse, specular reflection (Phong model); Flat shading, Gouraud shading, Phong shading; Introduction to Ray Tracing and OpenGL.

textbooks.authors: Donald Hearn, M. Pauline Baker, Warren Carithers
textbooks.title: Computer Graphics with OpenGL

referenceBooks.title: Interactive Computer Graphics: A Top-Down Approach with WebGL

CSE-4872.courseRationale: Practical programming of 2D and 3D graphics applications using C++/OpenGL/GLUT.
objectives: Implement graphics algorithms (Bresenham, transformations, clipping) in C++.
Use modern OpenGL shader pipelines and GLUT libraries for interactive 3D rendering.
Develop interactive 2D/3D games or graphic simulations.

clos.description: Implement raster line, circle, and polygon drawing algorithms.
Apply matrix transformations and user interaction in OpenGL.
Design textured, illuminated 3D scenes with camera controls.

midtermContent.topic: Setting up OpenGL and GLUT environment; drawing basic 2D primitives (points, lines, quads, polygons).
Implementing Bresenham's line and Midpoint circle drawing algorithms without OpenGL built-in functions.
2D transformations implementation: Moving, rotating, and scaling geometric objects using keyboard/mouse callbacks.

finalContent.topic: Cohen-Sutherland line clipping algorithm visualization.
3D geometric modeling: rendering 3D cubes, pyramids, spheres with gluPerspective.
Lighting, material properties, and camera navigation in OpenGL.
Term Project: 2D/3D Interactive game or simulation with collision detection.

CSE-4875.courseRationale: Covers digital representation, enhancement, restoration, segmentation, and feature extraction of image data in spatial and frequency domains.
objectives: Understand sampling, quantization, pixel relationships, and spatial filtering.
Master Fourier transform applications in 2D image filtering and restoration.
Apply morphological operations, image thresholding, edge detection, and segmentation.

clos.description: Explain fundamental steps in digital image processing, sampling, quantization, and spatial intensity transformations.
Design spatial and frequency domain filters for image enhancement, noise smoothing, and sharpening.
Formulate image restoration degradation models, inverse filtering, and Wiener filtering.
Apply morphological operations (dilation, erosion, opening, closing) and edge/threshold segmentation algorithms.

midtermContent.topic: Introduction: Steps in DIP, image acquisition, sampling, quantization, resolution, pixel adjacency and connectivity.
Spatial Intensity Transformations: Image negatives, log transforms, power-law (gamma) transformations, piecewise-linear functions, histogram equalization and matching.
Spatial Filtering: Spatial correlation and convolution; Smoothing linear and non-linear filters (order-statistic, median); Sharpening filters (Laplacian, Unsharp masking).

finalContent.topic: Frequency Domain Filtering: 2D Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT), Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), Ideal, Butterworth, and Gaussian lowpass and highpass filters.
Image Restoration & Reconstruction: Noise models (Gaussian, Rayleigh, salt-and-pepper), restoration in spatial/frequency domains, Inverse and Wiener filtering.
Color Image Processing: RGB, CMYK, HSI color models, pseudocolor processing, full-color image smoothing and sharpening.
Morphological Image Processing: Structuring elements, erosion, dilation, opening, closing, hit-or-miss transform, boundary extraction, hole filling.
Image Segmentation: Detection of discontinuities (Sobel, Prewitt, Canny edge detectors), thresholding (Otsu's method), region-based segmentation, watershed algorithm.

textbooks.authors: Rafael C. Gonzalez, Richard E. Woods
textbooks.title: Digital Image Processing

referenceBooks.title: Digital Image Processing: PIKS Scientific Inside

CSE-2430.courseRationale: Full-stack web application development: semantic HTML5, modern CSS3 layout systems (Flexbox, Grid), JavaScript (ES6+), DOM manipulation, asynchronous programming (Fetch/AJAX), and backend server development with RESTful APIs.
objectives: Build responsive and accessible web interfaces adhering to modern web standards.
Develop interactive clients using vanilla JavaScript and DOM APIs.
Build RESTful backend APIs and integrate with databases.

clos.description: Create responsive, accessible user interfaces using semantic HTML5 and modern CSS3.
Implement interactive client-side logic using modern JavaScript, event listeners, and async APIs.
Construct RESTful API services connecting backend servers to databases with authentication.

midtermContent.topic: Web architecture, HTTP protocol, HTML5 semantic elements, forms, accessibility (ARIA).
Modern CSS3: Box model, Flexbox, CSS Grid layout, responsive media queries, CSS variables, dark mode.
JavaScript Essentials: Data structures, arrow functions, DOM querying, event handling, local storage.

finalContent.topic: Asynchronous JavaScript: Promises, async/await, Fetch API, consuming JSON REST services.
Server-side programming with Node.js/Express or Spring Boot REST APIs.
Database connectivity (CRUD operations, SQL/NoSQL), session management, JWT authentication.
Capstone Full-Stack Project: End-to-end responsive web application deployment.

textbooks.title: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites

CSE-3529.courseRationale: Covers native and cross-platform mobile application design, lifecycle management, UI layout, local persistence (Room/SQLite), REST integration, background services, and hardware sensors.
objectives: Understand mobile OS architectures, activity lifecycles, and fragment management.
Design user interfaces adhering to Material Design principles.
Implement background tasks, offline caching, and REST API integration.

clos.description: Construct mobile layouts using modern UI components, ConstraintLayout, and Material Design.
Manage activity/fragment lifecycles, intents, navigation, and state preservation.
Integrate local storage, background workers, notifications, and network API consumption.

midtermContent.topic: Mobile platforms overview, Android Studio setup, project structure, Activity lifecycle.
UI Design: Layouts (Linear, Relative, Constraint), Views, RecyclerView, adapters, event listeners.
Inter-component communication: Explicit and implicit intents, passing data with Bundles, Fragment transactions.

finalContent.topic: Data persistence: SharedPreferences, Room database / SQLite ORM, LiveData, ViewModel.
Networking: Retrofit/Volley, JSON parsing, asynchronous background threading (Coroutines/Threads).
Sensors, GPS location services, Google Maps API, push notifications with Firebase.
Capstone Mobile App: Architecture design, testing, building APK, deployment.

textbooks.authors: Bill Phillips, Chris Stewart, Kristin Marsicano
textbooks.title: Android Programming: The Big Nerd Ranch Guide

MDP-3505.courseRationale: Equips students with foundational ethics, ethical paradigms, personal integrity, social responsibility, professional work ethics, and Islamic moral values for holistic character development.
objectives: Understand the philosophical foundations of morality, ethics, and character building.
Cultivate personal integrity, honesty, empathy, and social accountability.
Apply moral values in university life, professional engineering contexts, and society.

clos.description: Explain fundamental concepts of morality, conscience, values, and universal moral principles.
Analyze contemporary moral dilemmas, professional ethics, academic honesty, and social justice.
Formulate personal and professional codes of conduct rooted in moral development.

midtermContent.topic: Introduction: Definition of Morals, Ethics, Character, and Human Nature; The source of values.
Personal Integrity: Truthfulness, trustworthiness (Amanah), self-discipline, and fulfillment of covenants.
Academic Honesty: Ethics of learning, intellectual property, avoiding plagiarism, and respectful peer interactions.

finalContent.topic: Interpersonal Ethics: Empathy, kindness to parents, relatives, neighbors, and elder respect.
Social Responsibility: Environmental stewardship, public welfare, combating corruption and injustice.
Professional Ethics: Workplace accountability, ethical computing, confidentiality, and engineering responsibility.
Character Synthesis: Living a purpose-driven life, moral consistency, and continuous spiritual development.

textbooks.authors: IIUC Center for Moral and Spiritual Development
textbooks.title: Foundations of Moral Character and Professional Ethics
